start.text: Good evening. Do you have a table for one?

choices.text: Good evening! Yes, right this way. Here is the menu.
choices.tip: Polite greeting! Repeating the customer's greeting ('Good evening') and using 'right this way' sounds professional and welcoming.

choices.text: Yeah, just sit anywhere.
choices.tip: Too casual. 'Yeah' and 'just sit anywhere' sound careless. Try: 'Yes, of course. Please follow me.'

menu.text: Thank you. I'm quite hungry, but I'm not very familiar with Japanese food. What do you recommend?

choices.text: Our Salmon Nigiri Set is very popular. It's fresh and delicious.
choices.tip: Great recommendation! Use 'popular' and two adjectives ('fresh and delicious') to make food sound attractive.

choices.text: The Ikura Gunkan is a chef's favourite. It's rich and a little salty.
choices.tip: Nice! 'A chef's favourite' makes the dish sound special. Describing taste ('rich', 'a little salty') helps the customer decide.

choices.text: Before I recommend something, is there anything you don't eat?
choices.tip: Excellent service! Asking about food the customer doesn't eat is polite and shows you care. 'Is there anything you don't eat?' is a very useful question.

choices.text: I don't know, everything is good. Just pick something.
choices.tip: Unhelpful. The customer asked for advice. 'I don't know' and 'just pick something' sound lazy. Try: 'I'd recommend…'

vocab.meaning: knowing something well because you have seen or used it before
to suggest something because you think it is good

recommend_salmon.text: That sounds great! I love salmon. Does the set come with anything else?

choices.text: Yes, it includes a bowl of hot miso soup and a small salad.
choices.tip: Clear answer! 'It includes…' is a useful phrase to explain what comes with a set meal.

choices.text: No. Just the sushi.
choices.tip: Too short. A one-word 'No' sounds cold. Try: 'It comes with miso soup. Would you like to add a salad?'

vocab.meaning: a meal with several dishes served together for one price

drink.text: Perfect. Could I also get something to drink?

choices.text: Of course! Would you prefer hot green tea or cold water?
choices.tip: Great! 'Would you prefer A or B?' is a polite way to offer choices and helps the customer decide quickly.

choices.text: The drinks are in the fridge. Get it yourself.
choices.tip: Rude! Customers expect you to serve them. Try: 'Of course. What would you like to drink?'

recommend_ikura.text: Ikura? I've never heard of it. What is it exactly?

choices.text: It's salmon roe. They're small orange fish eggs that pop in your mouth.
choices.tip: Very clear! Explaining a new food with simple words, colour and texture ('small', 'orange', 'pop') makes it easy to understand.

choices.text: Fish eggs. Do you want it or not?
choices.tip: Impatient. 'Do you want it or not?' sounds pushy. Try: 'It's salmon roe. Would you like to try it?'

vocab.meaning: used to ask for more detail or a clear answer

ikura_reply.text: Interesting! I'd like to try something new. I'll have the Ikura Gunkan, please.

choices.text: Excellent choice. Coming right up!
choices.tip: 'Excellent choice' compliments the customer, and 'Coming right up!' is a friendly way to say the food will be ready soon.

vocab.meaning: to do or eat something for the first time

order_confirmed_ikura.text: I can't wait to try it!

ask_diet.text: Thank you for asking! Actually, I'm vegetarian, so I don't eat fish or meat.

choices.text: No problem! Our Avocado Cucumber Roll has no fish at all. It's fresh and crunchy.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'No problem!' makes the customer feel comfortable, and you offered a suitable dish right away.

choices.text: Sushi without fish? That's a bit strange.
choices.tip: Impolite. Never judge a customer's diet. Respect their choice and help: 'Of course. We have a vegetable roll.'

vocab.meaning: a person who does not eat meat or fish

veggie_happy.text: Wonderful! That sounds delicious. I'll have the Avocado Cucumber Roll.

choices.text: Great choice. I'll make sure there's no fish in it.
choices.tip: Good! Repeating the customer's request ('no fish') shows you listened carefully.

veggie_upset.text: It's not strange, it's my choice. Do you have anything without fish or not?

choices.text: I'm sorry, that was rude of me. We have an Avocado Cucumber Roll.
choices.tip: Good recovery! A sincere apology ('I'm sorry, that was rude of me') can fix a mistake. Then offer a solution.

choices.text: Fine. There's a vegetable roll.
choices.tip: Still unfriendly. 'Fine.' sounds annoyed. Apologise first, then offer the dish politely.

order_confirmed_veggie.text: Thank you. I'm looking forward to it.

vocab.meaning: feeling happy and excited about something that will happen

recommend_bad.text: Oh... well, I guess I'll just have the Tuna Nigiri then.

choices.text: Tuna it is. I'll get that for you.
choices.tip: This is OK, but the customer is already disappointed. Adding an apology helps: 'Sorry about that. Tuna is a great choice.'

wasabi.text: Is the green paste spicy? I'm not good with spicy food.

choices.text: Yes, that's wasabi. I can leave it out for you if you like.
choices.tip: Very helpful! 'I can leave it out' offers to change the dish. 'If you like' makes the offer polite.

choices.text: It's not that spicy. You'll be fine.
choices.tip: Ignoring the customer's concern is not good service. Offer to change the dish: 'I can make it without wasabi.'

vocab.meaning: a soft, thick mixture
having a hot, strong taste that burns your mouth a little

order_confirmed_tuna_plain.text: Thank you, that's very kind. No wasabi, please!

vocab.meaning: friendly and helpful

order_confirmed_salmon.text: I'm looking forward to the meal!

vocab.meaning: feeling happy and excited about something that will happen

order_confirmed_tuna.text: Please don't take too long, I'm in a hurry.

vocab.meaning: needing to do something quickly because you don't have much time

ikura_bad.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound very nice. I'll just have a Salmon Roll instead.

choices.text: Of course. Sorry, I should have explained it better.
choices.tip: Good recovery! 'I should have…' is a polite way to admit a mistake.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but very short. Add something friendly: 'Of course. A Salmon Roll coming right up!'

vocab.meaning: in place of something else

order_confirmed_salmon_roll.text: Thanks. Please don't make me wait too long.

start.text: Ciao! It smells amazing in here. I am absolutely famished!

choices.text: Welcome to Bella Trattoria! Can I start you off with some drinks?
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Can I start you off with…?' is a polite, natural way to offer drinks first.

choices.text: Are you ready to order or do you need a minute?
choices.tip: This sounds rushed. The customer just sat down. Give them time and welcome them first.

vocab.meaning: extremely hungry

drinks.text: Just sparkling water with lemon, please. What is your signature dish?

choices.text: Our classic wood-fired Margherita Pizza is a favourite: tomato, mozzarella and fresh basil.
choices.tip: Great! Naming the main ingredients helps the customer imagine the dish.

choices.text: If you like mushrooms, our Mushroom Pizza is very popular.
choices.tip: Nice! 'If you like…' is a friendly way to suggest something that matches the customer's taste.

choices.text: Pizza is pizza. Just pick one.
choices.tip: Rude. The customer asked for your advice. Try: 'I'd recommend our Margherita.'

vocab.meaning: the special dish a restaurant is most famous for

rushing.text: I just sat down! But fine, I will just take a Margherita Pizza.

choices.text: Sorry to rush you. One Margherita Pizza coming right up.
choices.tip: Good recovery! Saying sorry quickly fixes the mistake.

choices.text: Yes, it is. There's no meat in it at all.
choices.tip: Clear and confident. 'No meat at all' answers the question completely.

choices.text: Probably.
choices.tip: Not sure is not good enough when a customer asks about food. Check, then answer clearly.

vocab.meaning: without any meat or fish

funghi.text: I love mushrooms! Are they fresh?

choices.text: Yes, we get fresh mushrooms from the market every morning.
choices.tip: Excellent! A detail like 'from the market every morning' makes your answer believable.

choices.text: They come from a can.
choices.tip: Honest, but it doesn't sell the dish. Focus on something good: 'They're cooked with garlic and herbs.'

vocab.meaning: recently picked or made, not old

bad.text: Oh... all right. A Margherita, then.

choices.text: Sorry about that. A Margherita it is!
choices.tip: Good recovery! A short apology and a cheerful confirmation.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but an apology would help after being rude.

crispy_margherita.text: Perfetto! Please make sure the crust is nice and crispy.

vocab.meaning: the hard outside edge of a pizza or bread
hard and dry in a pleasant way, making a sound when you bite it

crispy_funghi.text: Perfetto! Please make sure the crust is nice and crispy.

vocab.meaning: the hard outside edge of a pizza or bread
hard and dry in a pleasant way, making a sound when you bite it

start.text: Sawasdee krub! It's my first time at this market. What would you recommend for someone who loves strong flavors?

vocab.meaning: to say that something is good and someone should try it
the tastes that food has, such as sweet, salty or sour

choices.text: Sawasdee krub, welcome! If you love strong flavors, I'd recommend our Som Tam Poo.
choices.tip: Excellent! You greeted him back in Thai and used 'If you love…, I'd recommend…' to give a recommendation that matches what he wants.

choices.text: We have som tam. It's popular.
choices.tip: Correct, but very short. Try connecting your answer to what he asked: 'If you love strong flavors, I'd recommend…'

choices.text: Everything here is strong. Just choose something.
choices.tip: Rude. 'Just choose something' tells the customer you don't want to help. A server's job is to help guests choose.

rude_start.text: Hmm, that's not very helpful. Fine, I'll have the Som Tam Poo, I guess.

choices.text: I'm sorry about that, sir. It's a great choice. Let me tell you a little about it.
choices.tip: Good recovery! 'I'm sorry about that' accepts the problem, and offering more information shows you want to help now.

choices.text: OK, one Som Tam Poo.
choices.tip: Polite enough, but you missed the chance to apologize for your first answer.

choices.text: Good. It's the cheapest one anyway.
choices.tip: Talking about price like this can sound like you think the customer is cheap. Focus on why the dish is good.

describe.text: Som Tam Poo? I've never tried it. Could you describe it for me?

vocab.meaning: to say what something is like

choices.text: Of course. It's a green papaya salad with salted crab. It tastes salty, sour and spicy at the same time.
choices.tip: Perfect description! You named the main ingredients and used taste words (salty, sour, spicy) joined by 'at the same time'.

choices.text: It's papaya salad with crab.
choices.tip: True, but a description should also say how it tastes. Add adjectives like 'salty, sour and spicy'.

choices.text: It's hard to explain. Just try it.
choices.tip: Unhelpful. The customer asked you to describe the dish, so give him some details.

ingredients.text: Salted crab sounds interesting. Is the crab raw, or is it cooked?

vocab.meaning: not cooked

choices.text: The crab is salted, not cooked, which gives the salad its special taste. Is that OK for you?
choices.tip: Very good. You answered clearly, explained why ('which gives…'), and checked that it's OK for him. Checking is polite and safe.

choices.text: It's salted.
choices.tip: Correct but incomplete. He asked 'raw or cooked?', so answer that part too.

choices.text: Why does it matter? Everyone eats it.
choices.tip: Never question why a customer asks about food. Some people can't eat raw food for health reasons.

spice.text: That's fine with me. How spicy can you make it? I usually prefer my food quite hot.

vocab.meaning: to like one thing more than another
fairly; more than a little

choices.text: We can make it as spicy as you like. One chili is mild, and three chilies is Thai spicy.
choices.tip: Great! 'As spicy as you like' gives him the choice, and you explained the levels clearly with numbers.

choices.text: I can add more chilies.
choices.tip: OK, but give him clear options so he can decide how spicy he wants it.

choices.text: Thai spicy is probably too much for you.
choices.tip: Don't decide for the customer. This sounds like you think he can't handle it.

choose_level.text: Three chilies, please. Thai spicy! Is there anything you'd suggest eating with it?

vocab.meaning: to give an idea for someone to think about

choices.text: Sticky rice goes perfectly with som tam, and it helps if the salad feels too hot.
choices.tip: Very helpful! 'Goes perfectly with' is a natural way to pair foods, and you gave a useful reason.

choices.text: You can have sticky rice if you want.
choices.tip: Fine. Saying why it goes well together would make the suggestion stronger.

choices.text: No, that's enough food.
choices.tip: He asked for a suggestion, so 'that's enough food' sounds like you are judging how much he eats.

confirm.text: Wonderful. One Som Tam Poo with three chilies, please. I can't wait to try it!

vocab.meaning: to be very excited about something that will happen soon

start.text: Bonjour! What a charming café. Do you have any seasonal desserts today?

vocab.meaning: pleasant and attractive
available only at a particular time of year

choices.text: Bonjour, madame! Yes, this season we're serving a Berry Macaron Tower with fresh strawberries.
choices.tip: Lovely! You greeted her in her style ('Bonjour, madame') and answered with a specific seasonal dessert.

choices.text: We have a macaron tower.
choices.tip: Correct, but it doesn't sound special. Mention why it's seasonal, for example the fresh berries.

choices.text: Everything is in the display case. You can look yourself.
choices.tip: Unwelcoming. 'You can look yourself' tells the guest you won't help. Offer to explain the desserts instead.

rude_start.text: Oh... I was hoping for a little help. What is the macaron tower, then?

choices.text: I apologize, madame. It's a tower of pink, green and yellow macarons with fresh berries on top.
choices.tip: Good recovery. 'I apologize' is more formal than 'sorry' and suits a café like this one.

choices.text: It's macarons in a tower.
choices.tip: Too short. Describe the colors or the berries to make it sound attractive.

choices.text: It's the tall one in the case.
choices.tip: She asked what it is, not where it is. Describe the dessert.

describe.text: How lovely! Could you tell me what the macarons are made of?

vocab.meaning: the materials or ingredients used to make something

choices.text: Certainly. They're made of almond flour, egg whites and sugar, and we put fresh berries on top.
choices.tip: Excellent. 'Certainly' is a polite word for 'yes', and you listed the ingredients clearly.

choices.text: Macarons and berries.
choices.tip: This doesn't answer 'made of'. Name the ingredients: almond flour, egg whites, sugar.

choices.text: I'm not sure. The baker makes them.
choices.tip: Staff should know the menu. If you really don't know, say 'Let me check for you.'

sweetness.text: It sounds wonderful, but is it very sweet? I don't really enjoy desserts that are too sugary.

vocab.meaning: containing a lot of sugar

choices.text: The macarons are sweet, but the berries are slightly sour, so the flavor is nicely balanced.
choices.tip: Great B1 language! 'X, but Y, so Z' explains a contrast and its result in one sentence.

choices.text: It's a little sweet.
choices.tip: OK. Explaining why it isn't too sweet would make her feel more confident.

choices.text: It's a dessert. Of course it's sweet.
choices.tip: This sounds like you think her question is silly. Answer the concern she has.

drink.text: That sounds perfect. Which drink would you suggest to go with it?

vocab.meaning: to taste or look good together

choices.text: I'd suggest Earl Grey tea. Its light flavor pairs beautifully with the berries.
choices.tip: Very elegant. 'I'd suggest…' is a polite recommendation, and 'pairs with' is used for food and drink that taste good together.

choices.text: Tea or coffee is fine.
choices.tip: She asked for your suggestion, so choose one and give a reason.

choices.text: Whatever you want. The drinks are on the menu.
choices.tip: 'Whatever you want' sounds like you don't care. Make a real suggestion.

occasion.text: Merci. Oh, it's my granddaughter's birthday today. Would it be possible to add a candle?

vocab.meaning: a very polite way to ask for something
a stick of wax that you light, often put on a birthday cake

choices.text: How wonderful! Of course, I'd be happy to add a candle. Please wish her a happy birthday from us.
choices.tip: Warm and professional. 'I'd be happy to…' agrees to a request politely, and the birthday wish is a kind touch.

choices.text: Yes, we can add one.
choices.tip: Fine, but a special occasion is a chance to be extra friendly.

choices.text: We don't usually do that.
choices.tip: If something is unusual but possible, try to help anyway. Small kindnesses make guests come back.

confirm.text: Wonderful. One Berry Macaron Tower and a pot of Earl Grey, please.

start.text: Hey there! I'm absolutely starving. What's the best thing on your menu?

vocab.meaning: very hungry (informal)
completely; used to make a word stronger

choices.text: Welcome to Route 66! Our Classic Cheeseburger is the most popular dish we serve.
choices.tip: Great welcome. The superlative 'the most popular' is a strong way to recommend something.

choices.text: People usually order the cheeseburger.
choices.tip: Helpful, but add a welcome and make it sound exciting.

choices.text: Burgers. It's a diner.
choices.tip: This sounds like the question was stupid. Every guest deserves a friendly answer.

rude_start.text: Wow, okay. I guess I'll have the cheeseburger, then.

choices.text: Sorry, that came out wrong. Our cheeseburger is excellent, and I'll make it fresh for you.
choices.tip: Good recovery. 'That came out wrong' is a natural way to apologize for how you said something.

choices.text: One cheeseburger.
choices.tip: Correct, but she sounds a little hurt. An apology would help.

choices.text: Good. It's quick to make.
choices.tip: This makes it sound like you chose for your own convenience, not for the customer.

recommend.text: Sounds great. What exactly comes with it?

vocab.meaning: is served together with

choices.text: It comes with a grilled beef patty, melted cheese, lettuce and tomato on a toasted bun.
choices.tip: Excellent detail. Past participles like 'grilled', 'melted' and 'toasted' make food sound delicious.

choices.text: Beef, cheese and vegetables.
choices.tip: Correct, but a little plain. Describe how each part is cooked.

choices.text: The normal burger things.
choices.tip: Too vague. She asked 'what exactly', so give exact details.

cook.text: How do you cook the patty? I really don't like it pink inside.

vocab.meaning: a flat, round piece of meat for a burger

choices.text: We season it and grill it on both sides until it's cooked all the way through.
choices.tip: Clear process language: 'until it's cooked all the way through' answers her worry exactly.

choices.text: We grill it well.
choices.tip: OK. Explaining that it won't be pink inside would reassure her more.

choices.text: Pink is how it's supposed to be.
choices.tip: Don't tell a customer their preference is wrong. Cook it the way she likes.

hold.text: Perfect. Oh, and could you hold the lettuce? I'm not a fan.

vocab.meaning: don't put lettuce on it
don't like something very much

choices.text: Absolutely. One cheeseburger with no lettuce. Is there anything else I can get you?
choices.tip: Professional. You repeated the order to confirm it and offered more help.

choices.text: OK, no lettuce.
choices.tip: Correct. Repeating the whole order helps avoid mistakes.

choices.text: Lettuce is healthy, you know. I'll leave it on.
choices.tip: Ignoring a request is a serious service mistake. You can share an opinion, but do what the customer asks.

wait.text: That's all, thanks. I'm in a bit of a hurry, though. How long is the wait right now?

vocab.word: in a bit of a hurry
vocab.meaning: needing to do things a little quickly

choices.text: It's a little busy, but it'll be ready in about ten minutes. Thank you for your patience.
choices.tip: Excellent. You were honest about being busy, gave a time, and thanked her: 'Thank you for your patience.'

choices.text: Around ten minutes.
choices.tip: Clear. Thanking her for waiting would make it friendlier.

choices.text: We're busy. It'll be ready when it's ready.
choices.tip: This sounds annoyed and gives no real information.

wait_lettuce.text: Ugh, fine. Just be quick. I'm in a hurry.

choices.text: Of course. It'll be ready in about ten minutes.
choices.tip: Polite and clear. (But remember: next time, follow the customer's request!)

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Too short when the customer is unhappy.

choices.text: Everyone's in a hurry.
choices.tip: This makes the customer feel unimportant.

confirm_no_lettuce.text: Thanks! My stomach is rumbling already.

vocab.meaning: making a long, low sound, like a hungry stomach

confirm_lettuce.text: Whatever. My stomach is rumbling anyway.

vocab.meaning: making a long, low sound, like a hungry stomach

start.text: Hi! Sorry, I'm in a bit of a rush. How long does a sushi roll take?

choices.text: Hello! A roll takes about five minutes. Would you like one?
choices.tip: Great! Answer the question first with a clear time ('about five minutes'), then make an offer: 'Would you like one?'

choices.text: It depends. Why are you in a rush?
choices.tip: Too personal. The customer didn't ask for a chat. Just tell them the time: 'It takes about five minutes.'

vocab.meaning: a little busy and needing to do things quickly

menu.text: Five minutes is perfect. Which one do you recommend?

choices.text: The Salmon Roll is our best seller. It's fresh and simple.
choices.tip: Nice! 'Best seller' means many people buy it. It's a strong reason to choose a dish.

choices.text: The Tuna Nigiri is quick to make and very fresh today.
choices.tip: Good thinking! The customer is in a rush, so 'quick to make' answers what she really needs.

choices.text: Whatever. They're all the same.
choices.tip: Rude and unhelpful. 'Whatever' sounds like you don't care. Try: 'I'd recommend the Salmon Roll.'

vocab.meaning: to suggest something because you think it is good

salmon_side.text: Great, a Salmon Roll then. Could I have extra soy sauce on the side?

choices.text: Of course. I'll put some soy sauce on the side for you.
choices.tip: Perfect! Repeating the request ('soy sauce on the side') shows you listened.

choices.text: Soy sauce is already on the table.
choices.tip: Not wrong, but a bit cold. Friendlier: 'Sure! There's some on the table, and I can bring you more.'

vocab.meaning: served separately, not on top of the food

tuna_side.text: Sounds good. Is the tuna fresh today?

choices.text: Yes, it arrived this morning. It's very fresh.
choices.tip: Excellent! Giving a fact ('it arrived this morning') makes your answer believable.

choices.text: I think so.
choices.tip: Unsure answers worry customers. If you know, say it clearly: 'Yes, it's very fresh.'

vocab.meaning: recently made, caught or picked, not old

bad.text: Oh... OK. Then just a Salmon Roll, please. Quickly.

choices.text: Sorry about that. One Salmon Roll, coming right up!
choices.tip: Good recovery! A quick apology and 'coming right up' show you'll be fast.

choices.text: Fine.
choices.tip: Still unfriendly. Apologise first: 'Sorry about that. I'll make it quickly.'

start.text: Good evening, young man. Could you speak a little slowly, please? My hearing isn't very good.

choices.text: Of course. Good evening. Please take your time.
choices.tip: Kind and clear! Short, simple sentences are easier to hear. 'Please take your time' is very polite.

choices.text: WHAT WOULD YOU LIKE?!
choices.tip: Shouting sounds rude. Speak slowly and clearly, not loudly.

vocab.meaning: the ability to hear sounds

menu.text: Thank you, dear. I'd like something soft. My teeth aren't very strong.

choices.text: Would you like the Ikura Gunkan? The salmon roe is soft and easy to eat.
choices.tip: Great! You listened to her need ('soft') and explained why the dish fits: 'easy to eat'.

choices.text: The Tuna Nigiri is very soft and tender.
choices.tip: Good! 'Tender' is a useful word for food that is soft and easy to bite.

choices.text: Sushi is all the same. Just eat it.
choices.tip: Very rude. Never tell a customer 'just eat it'. Help them choose: 'This one is soft.'

vocab.meaning: not hard; easy to press or bite

ikura.text: That sounds lovely. Is it very salty?

choices.text: Just a little. Would you like some green tea with it?
choices.tip: Nice! You answered and then offered something extra. Green tea goes well with salty food.

choices.text: Yes. Very salty.
choices.tip: True, but very short. Add something helpful: 'A little. Green tea goes well with it.'

vocab.meaning: tasting of salt

tuna.text: Lovely. Could you make it without wasabi, please? It's too strong for me.

choices.text: Certainly. I'll make it without wasabi.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Certainly' is a very polite 'yes', and you repeated her request.

choices.text: But wasabi is good for you.
choices.tip: Don't argue with a customer's request. Say: 'Certainly. No wasabi for you.'

vocab.meaning: having more taste than someone likes

bad.text: Oh dear. Then I'll have the Salmon Nigiri, I suppose.

choices.text: I'm sorry, madam. One Salmon Nigiri for you.
choices.tip: Good recovery! 'Madam' is a polite way to speak to an older woman.

choices.text: OK.
choices.tip: Acceptable, but an apology would help after being rude.

vocab.meaning: said when you agree but are not very happy about it
friendly and caring

start.text: Good evening, young man. Is the pasta fresh here?

choices.text: Good evening! Yes, we make it fresh every morning.
choices.tip: Great! A polite greeting plus a clear fact.

choices.text: It's from a packet, like everywhere.
choices.tip: This makes the food sound cheap. If you can, say something positive about it.

vocab.meaning: recently made, not old

menu.text: Wonderful. I'd like spaghetti, but nothing too spicy, please. And I like my pasta al dente.

choices.text: Our Spaghetti Pomodoro has a mild tomato sauce. It isn't spicy at all.
choices.tip: Perfect! 'Mild' is the opposite of 'spicy', and you showed you listened.

choices.text: You should try our chilli spaghetti. It's the best!
choices.tip: You didn't listen. She said 'nothing too spicy'. Always match your suggestion to the request.

vocab.meaning: having a hot, burning taste
cooked so it is still a little firm when you bite it

not_listening.text: I just said nothing spicy, young man.

choices.text: I'm sorry. Then I'd suggest the Spaghetti Pomodoro. It's mild.
choices.tip: Good recovery! Apologise, then give a suggestion that fits.

choices.text: Fine, the normal one, then.
choices.tip: It works, but it sounds annoyed. Add 'I'm sorry' first.

cheese.text: That sounds perfect. Could I have some extra cheese on top?

choices.text: Certainly. I'll add some grated Parmesan on top.
choices.tip: Excellent! 'Certainly' is a polite yes, and you repeated her request clearly.

choices.text: Cheese costs extra.
choices.tip: Talking about money first sounds unfriendly, and now she won't get her cheese. Say yes, then mention the price politely if needed.

vocab.meaning: placed on the highest part of something
friendly and caring

confirm_plain.text: Oh. Never mind the cheese, then.

vocab.meaning: said when you decide something is not important any more

start.text: Hi! Before I order, I need to tell you something important. I'm allergic to peanuts.

vocab.meaning: having a bad reaction to something you eat or touch
something you need to pay attention to

choices.text: Thank you for letting me know. I'll make sure there are no peanuts in your food.
choices.tip: Excellent. 'Thank you for letting me know' welcomes the information, and 'I'll make sure…' promises action.

choices.text: OK, no peanuts.
choices.tip: Correct, but for an allergy, a careful and reassuring answer is better: 'I'll make sure…'

choices.text: Just pick them out if you see any.
choices.tip: Dangerous and rude. A person with an allergy can get very sick from even a small piece. Always take allergies seriously.

upset.text: Picking them out isn't enough. Even a tiny piece could make me very sick!

vocab.meaning: very small

choices.text: I'm so sorry, you're right. I'll use clean tools and leave the peanuts out completely.
choices.tip: Good recovery. You apologized, agreed with her, and explained exactly what you will do.

choices.text: Fine, I won't add any.
choices.tip: 'Fine' sounds annoyed. Add an apology: 'I'm sorry, you're right.'

choices.text: I've never seen anyone get sick from it.
choices.tip: Never argue about allergies. The customer knows her body; your job is to keep her safe.

check.text: Thank you. Which salads on your menu are made without peanuts?

vocab.meaning: prepared with no amount of a certain ingredient

choices.text: Most of our salads use peanuts, but I can make the Som Tam Thai without them. It's sweet and sour.
choices.tip: Very good. You were honest ('most… use peanuts') and then offered a solution with 'but I can…'.

choices.text: Som Tam Thai, if I take out the peanuts.
choices.tip: Correct. Describing the dish would help her decide.

choices.text: All of them. That's how we make them.
choices.tip: This gives her no choice. Try to find a way to help: 'but I can make… without them.'

menu.text: Sweet and sour sounds lovely. What's in it?

vocab.meaning: tasting of sugar and of something like lime at the same time

choices.text: It has green papaya, dried shrimp, tomatoes, lime and palm sugar.
choices.tip: Clear and complete! Listing the ingredients helps a customer with allergies feel safe.

choices.text: Papaya and some other things.
choices.tip: 'Some other things' is not clear enough, especially for someone with an allergy. Name the ingredients.

choices.text: The usual stuff.
choices.tip: Too vague and too casual. She needs to know exactly what is in her food.

spice.text: Mmm. I'm not used to very spicy food, though. Can you make it mild?

vocab.meaning: not familiar with something because you don't do or have it often
not strong or not very spicy

choices.text: Of course. I'll use just one chili, so it will be mild but still tasty.
choices.tip: Perfect. 'Of course' is friendly, and 'so it will be…' explains the result of your choice.

choices.text: I'll use one chili.
choices.tip: Good answer. Adding 'Of course' makes it warmer.

choices.text: Som tam without chili isn't real som tam.
choices.tip: Don't criticize what the customer wants. Respect her preference.

confirm.text: Perfect. One Som Tam Thai, one chili and no peanuts. Thank you for being so careful!

vocab.meaning: giving attention to avoid mistakes or danger

start.text: Good morning! Am I too late for breakfast? Some cafés stop serving it at ten.

vocab.meaning: after the time when something can happen

choices.text: Good morning! Not at all. We serve breakfast until eleven, so you have plenty of time.
choices.tip: Great. 'Not at all' is a friendly answer, and 'so you have plenty of time' makes her feel relaxed.

choices.text: No, breakfast is until eleven.
choices.tip: Clear, but a little cold. Start with a greeting: 'Good morning!'

choices.text: You're almost late. Please order quickly.
choices.tip: This puts pressure on the customer. She still has time, so tell her that.

menu.text: Lucky me! I'm in the mood for something fluffy and sweet. What do you suggest?

vocab.meaning: wanting to have or do something at the moment
soft and light, full of air

choices.text: Our pancakes are light and fluffy, and they're served with butter and maple syrup.
choices.tip: Excellent. You repeated her word 'fluffy' and used the passive 'are served with' to describe the dish.

choices.text: We have pancakes.
choices.tip: Correct, but describe them so they sound delicious.

choices.text: Everything here is sweet. Just look at the menu.
choices.tip: She asked for your suggestion. Sending her to the menu is unhelpful.

time.text: Pancakes sound amazing! I have a meeting at nine thirty, though. How long will they take?

vocab.meaning: a time when people come together to talk about work or plans

choices.text: They'll be ready in about ten minutes, so you won't be late for your meeting.
choices.tip: Perfect. 'They'll be ready in about…' gives a clear time, and you connected it to her meeting.

choices.text: About ten minutes.
choices.tip: Clear and correct. Adding 'They'll be ready in…' sounds more natural.

choices.text: It depends. Maybe twenty minutes, maybe more.
choices.tip: Uncertain times make busy customers worried. Give your best clear estimate.

fruit.text: Great! And which fruit would you recommend on top?

vocab.meaning: placed on the highest part of something

choices.text: The strawberries are very fresh this week. They're sweet and juicy.
choices.tip: Good recommendation with a reason ('very fresh this week') and two adjectives.

choices.text: Blueberries are a great choice. They go really well with maple syrup.
choices.tip: Good recommendation. 'Go really well with' explains why they taste good together.

choices.text: I don't care. Just pick one.
choices.tip: 'I don't care' sounds rude. She asked for your opinion, so give one.

confirm_straw.text: Strawberries it is! Thank you so much.

confirm_blue.text: Mmm, blueberries! Thank you so much.

pick_blue.text: Oh... okay. Blueberries, then, I guess.

start.text: Howdy, partner! Just a side of fries for me. Last time I came here, they were cold.

vocab.meaning: a small extra dish served with a meal

choices.text: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll make sure your fries come out hot and crispy today.
choices.tip: Perfect complaint handling: say sorry ('I'm sorry to hear that') and promise to fix it ('I'll make sure…').

choices.text: They'll be hot today.
choices.tip: A promise is good, but start with an apology when a guest complains.

choices.text: That wasn't my shift.
choices.tip: Blaming someone else never helps. The guest just wants a good experience.

grumpy.text: Well, that's not much of an apology, is it?

vocab.meaning: words that say you are sorry

choices.text: You're right, and I apologize. I'll cook a fresh batch just for you.
choices.tip: Great recovery: agree ('You're right'), apologize, then offer something special.

choices.text: Sorry.
choices.tip: Better than nothing, but a real apology also says what you will do.

choices.text: I already said it wasn't me.
choices.tip: Arguing makes a complaint worse.

time.text: Alright. How long will they take? I'm meeting a friend at noon.

vocab.meaning: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day

choices.text: About ten minutes. We peel and cut the potatoes fresh, so they taste much better.
choices.tip: Excellent. You gave a time and explained why it's worth waiting.

choices.text: Ten minutes.
choices.tip: Correct and clear, but a little short.

choices.text: As long as it takes.
choices.tip: He told you he has plans. Give a clear time.

salt.text: Sounds good. Could you go easy on the salt? My doctor says I should cut down.

vocab.meaning: use only a little of something
to eat, drink or use less of something

choices.text: No problem. I'll leave the salt off, and you can add a little yourself if you want.
choices.tip: Very good. You agreed and gave him control: 'you can add a little yourself if you want.'

choices.text: OK, less salt.
choices.tip: Fine. 'No problem' sounds friendlier than 'OK'.

choices.text: Trust me, fries need salt.
choices.tip: This is a health request. Never ignore it.

sauce.text: Much appreciated. Do you have any sauces that aren't too salty?

vocab.meaning: something you are thankful for

choices.text: Our homemade tomato sauce has less salt than ketchup. Would you like to try some?
choices.tip: Great. You compared ('less salt than ketchup') and offered with 'Would you like to…?'

choices.text: We have ketchup and mayo.
choices.tip: This doesn't answer 'not too salty'. Compare the sauces for him.

choices.text: All sauces are salty.
choices.tip: Not true and not helpful. Look for an option that fits his needs.

sauce_salt.text: Well... I guess one time won't hurt.

confirm_no_salt.text: That'd be great. Much appreciated, partner.

vocab.meaning: thank you very much
